# Comparing Initializations

The `S3` and `S3b` series only differed in how much energy was placed
into kinetic energy (KE) (the `b` version generated $2N$ random numbers
and then multiplied them by a factor to set the KE to the requested
target). The potential energy (PE) was always at its minimum. This
appears valid, as even in the transition region (`S3.00295` was
diffusing; see @fig-S3.295all).

```{r}
#| label: fig-S3.295all
#| fig-cap: "Plot of first execution of `S3.00295`. The KE and PE can be seen to settle down quickly."
S3.00295.0000 <- readplot( paste(td, "S3.00295.0000.scalars.csv", sep="/"))
```

The KE quickly (200 steps) gives up its initial value of 0.0264 to
settle around 0.013022, while it rings for a short while, by the end of
the first 1,000 steps it has settled down.

```{r}
#| label: fig-S3.295z
#| fig-cap: "Zoom into @fig-S3.295all.  The solid line is the final average of the run computed over 4,0999k steps (only the first 1k steps were skipped)."
plot(S3.00295.0000$ke[1:1000], typ="l", xlab="step", ylab="ke", 
     panel.first=grid())
abline(h=MD2DF.P[run=="S3.00295",ke.mean.rs])
```

## PE of a Single Particle

```{r}
#| include: false
 x<-MD2DF.P[run=="S3.00295",.(ke.mean.rs, steps.avg, total.steps, TE.mean.rs, TE.sd.rs, TE.min.raw, TE.max.raw, pe.mean.rs)]
terng <- (x$TE.max.raw-x$TE.min.raw)/x$TE.mean.rs
```

Run `S3.00295` had a total per particle TE range (min to max) of
`r 100*terng`%. The average excess PE per particle (that is, the PE
above the minimum PE) is `r (pepp <- x$pe.mean.rs - 0.1159487884)` and
this is `r pepp/(terng*x$TE.mean.rs)` times the total TE range over 4M
steps. So while they are of the same order of magnitude, the per
particle share of that range is very small. The total available energy
is given by the KE of step zero, in which all of the added energy is
kinetic. This must be read from the text log, as the first step recorded
is the KE after the step. For this run, the value is 7.487, so the per
particle initialization KE is `r 7.487108031861905/256`, very close to
the desired initialization temperature of 0.0295 (which forms part of
the file name). The average excess PE of a single particle is therefore
`r 100 * pepp / (7.487108031861905 - pepp)`% of the total excess energy.

## Initializing PE

Version 1.3.4 of `MD2` added initialization ofthe PE, details recorded
in the Lab Notebook. The first official test run is below.

```{julia}

julia> td = abspath( @__DIR__, "..", "testdata")
"/media/phil/Original/Users/phils/Documents/DSP/MD/dev/testdata"

julia> @time MD2.runn( td, 10, "T4.", 1000, 5000, 5)
```

The code below creates @fig-T410 (the data is in a test directory which
gets cleaned out occasionally).

```{r}
#| label: T410
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
td2 <- "/media/phil/Original/Users/phils/Documents/DSP/MD/dev/testdata"
t4.0010.0000 <- readplot( paste(td2, "T4.0010.0000.scalars.csv", sep="/"))
pl <- recordPlot()
png("T410.png", width=600, height=300)
replayPlot(pl)
invisible(dev.off())
```

![Plot of first execution of `T4.0010`. The KE and PE can be seen to
settle down quickly.](T410.png){#fig-T410}

@fig-T410all below shows the full run.

```{r}
#| label: T410all
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
t4.0010 <- combineruns( td2, "T4", "0010", verbose=TRUE)
plot(t4.0010$rundt$ke, typ='l', panel.first = grid(), xlab="Step", 
     ylab="Energy / particle", main=" Kinetic and Excess Potential Energy")
lines(t4.0010$rundt$pe-0.1159487884, typ = 'l', col = 'red')
legend( 'topright', legend = c('KE', 'PE'), col = c( 'black', 'red'),
        lty=c(1, 1))
pl <- recordPlot()
png("T410all.png", width=600, height=300)
replayPlot(pl)
invisible(dev.off())
```

![Plot of all KE & excess PE points of `T4.0010`. The excess PE is a bit
higher than the KE in the fluid region.](T410all.png){#fig-T410all}

@fig-T410 shows the PE was clearly too high for the chosen temperature,
likely due to ignoring the positions of the particles when placing them:
particles randomly placed too close to each other will generate very
high energies. A "fudge factor" was introduced in version 1.3.5 which
altered the requested temperature for PE initialization. Using 0.5
(lowering the temperature by a factor of two) generated the following
results.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
julia> @time MD2.runn( td, 10, "T4b.", 1000, 5000, 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: T4b10all

t4b.0010 <- combineruns( td2, "T4b", "0010", verbose=TRUE)
plot(t4b.0010$rundt$ke, typ='l', panel.first = grid(), xlab="Step", 
     ylab="Energy / particle", main=" Kinetic and Excess Potential Energy")
lines(t4b.0010$rundt$pe-0.1159487884, typ = 'l', col = 'red')

        lty=c(1, 1))

png("T4b10all.png", width=600, height=300)
replayPlot(pl)
invisible(dev.off())
```

![Plot of all KE & PE points of `T4b.0010`. The lower initial PE caused
the temperature to be closer to the requested initialization temperature
of 0.01, so the excess substance is in the solid region and the PE and
KE are essentially mirror images of each other.](T4b10all.png)
